intuition: Search possible answer values rather than matrix positions. For a trial value, count how many entries are no larger than it. If that count is below k, the answer must be larger. Otherwise, keep that value and smaller candidates. Sorted rows and columns make the count efficient.

Count with a staircase starting at the bottom-left corner. A cell at most mid certifies every cell above it in that column, so add row+1 and move right. An oversized cell rules out that row position and everything to its right, so move upward.

The count grows monotonically with the proposed value, allowing binary search over the integer value interval. Search for the smallest threshold containing at least k entries. Duplicates count separately, and a threshold need not itself appear in the matrix during the search; the final threshold does.

At mid=12 in the worked matrix, start at row 2, column 0: value 12 qualifies, so add three entries and move right. Value 13 is too large, so move up to 11 and add two. At the last column, move up from 13 to 9 and add one.
The count is 3+2+1=6; the same sweep uses both upward moves and column-prefix additions.

steps: For matrix=[[1,5,9],[10,11,13],[12,13,15]] and k=8, initialize the candidate value range 1..15.
mid=8 admits only entries 1 and 5, so count=2<8. Raise low to 9.
mid=12 admits 1,5,9,10,11,12, giving count=6. Raise low again, now to 13.
With range 13..15, mid=14 admits eight entries, including both occurrences of 13. Set high=14.
mid=13 still admits eight entries, so set high=13. The boundaries coincide and the eighth value is 13.

codeNotes.note: Bottom-left is the useful corner: moving up decreases values, while moving right increases them, supporting one-way staircase progress.
Column sorting certifies all entries from row zero through this row, allowing an entire qualifying column prefix to be counted at once.
This compares rank information, not membership. Fewer than k qualifying entries proves the desired value lies above mid, even across value gaps.

keyDecision: Find the smallest value whose count of entries <= value is at least k. Count duplicates separately.
